Hi Sheila,

Thanks for getting in touch about the refund for order #KR-57340.

From what you've described, the refund is most likely not stuck. Refunds go back to the payment method the buyer used, and card refunds take 5 to 14 banking days to reach the buyer. Banking days don't include weekends or bank holidays, so 10 calendar days is usually fewer banking days than that. Your refund is probably still within the normal window.

The status will stay "Refund processing" until the card network confirms the refund. Until then, there's nothing more you need to do. Please don't refund the order a second time.

If the refund still shows "Refund processing" after 14 banking days, just let us know. We'll pass it to our payments team to look into.

You're welcome to share this with your buyer so she knows what to expect.

draft:
Hi Hector,

Thank you for being with us for almost four years, and for recommending Kariton to other shop owners in your collectors group. I'm sorry this has been such a frustrating stretch. I understand why a security warning is a serious problem when collectors are thinking about buying a PHP 80,000 watch, so let's get your domain working again.

The "Your connection is not private" warning means www.valdezvintage.example.com doesn't currently have a valid certificate from Kariton. Your nephew has already re-entered the DNS records, and the problem started right after you renewed the domain on October 7. Together, those point to a likely cause: when a domain is renewed or transferred, registrars sometimes add a CAA record to it without telling you. A CAA record says which certificate authorities can issue certificates for the domain. If it doesn't include Kariton's certificate authority, we can't issue a certificate for your shop.

Here's what to check at your domain registrar:

1. Look for a CAA record on the domain. If there is one, either remove it or add Kariton's certificate authority to it.

2. Check that no CDN or proxy feature is turned on at the registrar for the domain. If one is on, it can serve its own certificate instead of Kariton's.

3. Make sure the two DNS records are still set like this:
   CNAME, name "www", value "shops.kariton.test"
   A, name "@", value "203.0.113.10"

When that's done, go to Settings > Domains in your Kariton dashboard and click Retry certificate. That asks Kariton to issue the certificate again.

Your default address at <shop>.kariton.test keeps working the whole time, so you can send buyers there until the custom domain is fixed.

If the warning still appears after you click Retry certificate, just reply to this email. If you can, include a screenshot of the DNS records at your registrar, including any CAA records. We'll look into it further from there.

Thanks again for sticking with us, Hector.

Kariton Support
